item.location: approach.tex 'as in Morwani, a single-neuron optimization'
item.statement: Pricing amplitudes in norm reduces to a single-neuron optimization

chk.evidence:
I read Morwani et al., ICLR 2024 Spotlight, arXiv 2311.07568 v2, in full from the arXiv PDF and checked the venue on the abs page.

Sec 3.1, Lemma 3 (binary; proof in App E.1) and Sec 3.2, Lemma 5 (multi-class, class-weighted; App E.2) each have a 'Single neuron optimization' bullet. It says that for a fixed distribution q, any theta in argmax_{||theta||_{a,b}<=1} E_q[g(theta)] 'has directional support only on' Omega*_q = argmax_{||omega||_a<=1} E_q[psi(omega)]. The justification is that 'the expected margin of the network decomposes into the sum of expected margin of individual neurons', so E_q g = sum_i ||omega_i||^nu E_q psi(omega_i/||omega_i||) <= gamma max_{||w||_b<=1} ||w||_nu^nu. Combining neurons needs b = nu, and the Remark in App E.1 says other b values do not give the flexibility needed to satisfy Eq. 1. These lemmas serve the certificate-pair method (Lemma 2 / Lemma 6). Thm 7 applies it by maximising sum_j u^(j) v^(j) w^(-j) over one unit neuron.

What is shared: a network sum is reduced by homogeneity to a single unit-norm neuron problem.

What differs:
- Morwani's per-neuron objective is a linear expected margin under a dual q, used for a primal-dual certificate at b = nu.
- The paper's C_b = max_{||omega||<=1} sum_j |beta_j(omega)|^{b/nu} is a concave l_{b/nu} budget. It feeds a subadditivity upper bound for all 2 <= b <= nu and uses no dual distribution.

So 'as in Morwani' fits the decomposition idea but not their lemma as stated. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c11-morwani-single-neuron/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Lemmas 3 and 5 ('Single neuron optimization') support the reduction of a network-level objective to a unit-norm single-neuron maximisation via per-neuron additivity and homogeneity. Keep the citation, but point to those lemmas and say the objective differs.

chk.recommended_change: In approach.tex line 54, replace "It remains to price amplitudes in norm, which, as in \citet{morwani2024feature}, is a single-neuron optimization." with "It remains to price amplitudes in norm. As in the single-neuron step of \citet[Lemmas 3 and 5]{morwani2024feature}, homogeneity reduces this to one neuron. Here the per-neuron quantity is an $\ell_{b/\nu}$ budget of its Fourier coefficients rather than an expected margin under a dual distribution."
